chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Asking for a station wagon, and the Senator's trouble with the government
summary: The Senator, under government pressure over fake Hadacol testimonials, asked Danny to write up his block-dance plan and send it to Lafayette.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I said, 'Senator, we're having a problem with this van we got. We don't have transportation.' And my Uncle Paul

said, "Yeah, I've been in Lafayette, and I've seen all them station wagons you've got, all them trucks, and we can do something timed that we do with the Hadicol, and we'll use your truck to publicize your..."

He said, "Well, I'll tell you, we can't do that so well now, because I'm having a problem." He said, "You see, this Hadicol product I got is wonderful. It's one of the greatest folk...nature medicines that the world has ever known." He's a medicine man; he's selling it to us, too. He said, "But the government's breathing down my neck." That's the way he's talking. He said, "I've got to produce..." He used to put in the paper, have all them old people that's sick in there saying, "I drink Hadicol(?) and it's Hadicol(?) that preserved me, and I'm beginning to get well" -- you know, testimonials from people. There were about twenty people in the Times-Picayune sometimes, with these big ads. "See, now, the government's down my neck to produce these people. These people is dead. A lot of these people, I just picked them up and put them on there as a picture. And until I prove them, I can't do no more promoting of Hadicol(?). Since you came along with this thing here, this Hadicol girl..."
I said, "Also, I have a plan, Senator, that we could give block dances and we could go all over the South with

the bus." He said, "Have you got that down?" He said, "Write it down and send it to me. Here. Send it to Lafayette." I wrote the whole plan down to bring a whole transport truck loaded with small-sized Hadicol(?), large-sized Hadicol(?), that we'd have a caravan to go to every town, one night for White, one night for Colored, and we'd give block dances on (?) terms. And he said, "How would you do that?" I said, "We'd have a show. You get some Country-Western stars for the White people on the White nights, and they'll do their thing, and I'll do the thing for the Black people on the Black nights." He said, "My boy, that's a fantastic idea. Write it down, the way you would do that and send it to me.
